title: I'm begging you to start writing essays (even if you hate writing)

sentences.en: I am begging you to start writing more essays, or to just start writing essays, if you haven't already.
sentences.zh: 我求你了，开始写文章吧，如果你还没开始的话，现在就开始。

sentences.en: And no, I'm not talking about the essays that you were told to write in school.
sentences.zh: 我说的不是你上学时被要求写的那种文章。

sentences.en: I am talking about one of the greatest tools to learn faster.
sentences.zh: 我说的是能让你学得更快的最强工具之一。

sentences.en: Think deeper.
sentences.zh: 想得更深。

sentences.en: Improve the articulation of your ideas and beliefs and avoid being replaced by AI.
sentences.zh: 让你表达想法和信念时更清晰，并且避免被 AI 取代。

sentences.en: Yes, I'm serious, but those specifically are the selfish personal benefits of writing.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的，但这些只是写作给你个人带来的好处。

sentences.en: That's what you and I get from the act of putting words on paper.
sentences.zh: 是你我从把字写到纸上这个行为里得到的东西。

sentences.en: But there is something a lot deeper.
sentences.zh: 但还有更深层的东西。

sentences.en: The modern information environment is breaking our ability to think.
sentences.zh: 现代信息环境正在摧毁我们的思考能力。

sentences.en: And most people don't even notice.
sentences.zh: 大多数人甚至都没注意到。

sentences.en: And even more don't even care.
sentences.zh: 更多的人根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Essays might be one of the last forms of content that actually develops your capacity to make sense of reality, because right now we are living through the Large-Scale production of Fake Thinking in history, and the consequences of this are quite high, as you'll find out in this video, and only a select few of you will actually care enough to take advantage of it and profit from it.
sentences.zh: 文章可能是最后几种能真正培养你理解现实能力的内容形式之一，因为我们正在经历历史上最大规模的虚假思考生产，这件事的后果相当严重，你在这个视频里就会看到，而只有极少数人会真正在乎到去利用它、从中获利。

sentences.en: So in this video, I want to show you how this fake thinking epidemic, as we'll call it.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个视频里，我想让你看看这场虚假思考的流行病，我们就这么叫它吧。

sentences.en: And if it goes on as it is right now, which is in a bad downward direction, will not only make your own life worse, but will potentially lead to the collapse of civilization.
sentences.zh: 如果它照现在这样继续下去，也就是沿着一个糟糕的下坡路走，不仅会让你自己的生活变得更糟，还可能导致文明的崩溃。

sentences.en: And then at the end, I want to help you write your first essay so that you can fix one of the most precious resources that you have, which is your mind.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想帮你写出你的第一篇文章，这样你就能修复你拥有的最宝贵的资源之一，也就是你的头脑。

sentences.en: And of course, turning it into a career or a side income doesn't hurt either.
sentences.zh: 当然，把它变成一份事业或者一份副业收入也没什么坏处。

sentences.en: So the first point here is that the internet isn't dead, but it's killing us.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，互联网没有死，但它在杀死我们。

sentences.en: And we'll start with a quote from Daniel Stockton.
sentences.zh: 我们从 Daniel Stockton 的一句话开始。

sentences.en: Berger actually, every quote in this video is going to be from Daniel Stockton Berger.
sentences.zh: 其实是 Berger，这个视频里引用的每一句话都来自 Daniel Stockton Berger。

sentences.en: The written word as the primary type of media was probably required for democracy to work because it required the capacity to pay attention to an idea for long enough to understand it.
sentences.zh: 文字作为主要的媒介形式，可能是民主制度得以运转的必要条件，因为它要求你有能力把注意力放在一个想法上足够长的时间，直到真正理解它。

sentences.en: Now, the point of this section is that social media and I are quite literally a threat to civilization, and I know you don't see it as that, because all you see it as is this little app on your phone that you use every day.
sentences.zh: 这一部分的核心观点是，社交媒体和 AI 简直就是对文明的威胁，我知道你不这么看，因为你只把它当成手机上一个每天用的小应用。

sentences.en: And I know it sounds insane, like how could doom scrolling Instagram Reels eventually lead to the collapse of society?
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很疯狂，比如，无脑刷 Instagram Reels 怎么会最终导致社会崩溃？

sentences.en: How could watching a little person dance on TikTok hurt?
sentences.zh: 看一个小人在 TikTok 上跳舞能有什么害处？

sentences.en: How could reading someone's five second 280 character opinion polarizing opinion on Trump on Twitter ruin the world?
sentences.zh: 在 Twitter 上读一条某人用 280 个字符、花五秒钟发表的关于特朗普的极端观点，怎么能毁掉世界？

sentences.en: That's just something that you do on your lunch break.
sentences.zh: 那不过是你午休时干的事。

sentences.en: The reason is because you only focus on yourself.
sentences.zh: 原因在于你只关注你自己。

sentences.en: You only think about your own little bubble of life, and you don't think about the impact or the consequences of the little unconscious actions that you've picked up over time.
sentences.zh: 你只想着自己生活的小泡泡，不去想你长期以来养成的那些无意识的小行为会带来什么影响或后果。

sentences.en: And so when you zoom out beyond yourself to see what's really at play, it's hard to unsee.
sentences.zh: 所以当你把视角拉远，跳出自己去看真正在发生什么的时候，你就很难再视而不见了。

sentences.en: Now there are three layers to this.
sentences.zh: 这里面有三个层次。

sentences.en: So stick with me because we're going to go deep, and I promise that it will change the way that you think about not only writing and essays, but just long form content in general and social media and how actually impactful those things can be.
sentences.zh: 所以跟紧我，因为我们要深入了，我保证这会改变你思考的方式，不只是对写作和文章，而是对长内容、社交媒体，以及这些东西到底能有多大的影响力。

sentences.en: So the first layer is that the epistemic commons is being poisoned.
sentences.zh: 第一个层次是，认知公地正在被毒化。

sentences.en: So your question then is what is the epistemic comments?
sentences.zh: 那你可能会问，什么是认知公地？

sentences.en: And you can think of it as the water supply.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成供水系统。

sentences.en: But for information. So that's social media. That's the news.
sentences.zh: 但供的是信息。也就是社交媒体，是新闻。

sentences.en: That's wherever you get information from a public resource.
sentences.zh: 也就是你从任何公共资源获取信息的地方。

sentences.en: So as an example, most people watch the news to stay informed or to educate themselves.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，大多数人看新闻是为了了解时事或者自我教育。

sentences.en: But if you look closely you can just see that they're getting complacent.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细观察，就会发现他们只是在变得麻木。

sentences.en: They're not thinking at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有在思考。

sentences.en: Their lives aren't changing for the better.
sentences.zh: 他们的生活并没有变得更好。

sentences.en: In fact, more people are just becoming more jaded, more polarized, and more violent.
sentences.zh: 事实上，更多人只是变得更愤世嫉俗、更极端、更暴力。

sentences.en: Whenever you post on social media or whenever someone creates a TV show or movie, or whenever someone produces music on Spotify, the epistemic comments or public information environment grows.
sentences.zh: 每当你在社交媒体上发帖，或者有人制作电视节目或电影，或者有人在 Spotify 上发布音乐，认知评论或公共信息环境就会膨胀。

sentences.en: Now, this obviously gets very complex and it requires a certain level of systems thinking to completely understand.
sentences.zh: 这显然会变得非常复杂，需要一定程度的系统思维才能完全理解。

sentences.en: But if the content you publish in public hurts more than it helps, and is not counterbalanced by content that does help, our intellectual water source becomes contaminated.
sentences.zh: 但如果你公开发布的内容造成的伤害大于帮助，而且没有被真正有帮助的内容所平衡，我们的智识水源就会被污染。

sentences.en: So why is that bad?
sentences.zh: 那这为什么不好？

sentences.en: Because the information that you or any individual consumes influences your identity, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你或任何个体所消费的信息，会影响你的身份认同，对吧？

sentences.en: If you've watched any of my other videos on identity, or the self or personality or the psychology behind it all, you understand that your identity is created through this feedback loop of information that leads to conditioning, or information that leads to action, and once repeated, leads to conditioning, and that becomes who you are.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过我其他关于身份认同、自我、人格或背后心理学的视频，你就会明白，你的身份是通过信息的反馈循环创造出来的，这些信息导致条件反射，或者说信息导致行动，一旦重复，就形成条件反射，而这就成了你。

sentences.en: So your identity, which is shaped by the information that you consume, influences your behavior and thus your trajectory in life.
sentences.zh: 所以你的身份认同——由你消费的信息塑造——会影响你的行为，进而影响你的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: It determines the outcome of your life.
sentences.zh: 它决定你人生的结果。

sentences.en: You think something as simple as reading a little social media post doesn't determine where you end up in life.
sentences.zh: 你以为读一篇小小的社交媒体帖子这种简单的事，不会决定你最终走向哪里。

sentences.en: You are wrong.
sentences.zh: 你错了。

sentences.en: Now, beyond that, the form of information that you consume.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有你消费的信息形式。

sentences.en: So a short form tweet or long form books or articles or podcasts that trains your attention span.
sentences.zh: 短小的推文，还是长篇书籍、文章或播客，这些会训练你的注意力时长。

sentences.en: It also trains your tolerance for complexity and ability to hold contradictions in the capacity for nuance.
sentences.zh: 它也会训练你对复杂性的容忍度、容纳矛盾的能力，以及把握细微差别的能力。

sentences.en: And I mean, that's why you learn in the first place, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这本来就是你学习的初衷，对吧？

sentences.en: That's why you intentionally consume information.
sentences.zh: 这就是你有意识地消费信息的原因。

sentences.en: It's to equip yourself with the knowledge and cognitive capacity and ability to get what you want in life.
sentences.zh: 是为了用知识、认知能力和本领武装自己，去得到你在生活中想要的东西。

sentences.en: But that's just it.
sentences.zh: 但问题就在这儿。

sentences.en: Before you can solve any problem that is a civilizational threat in climate governance, AI alignment, public health, or the rest, you need a population capable of understanding the problem coherently.
sentences.zh: 在你能解决任何构成文明威胁的问题之前——无论是气候治理、AI 对齐、公共卫生还是其他——你需要一个能够连贯理解这些问题的人口。

sentences.en: 99% of people don't even know what these problems entail because they're happy drooling over the cat video on their phone.
sentences.zh: 99% 的人甚至不知道这些问题意味着什么，因为他们正开心地对着手机上的猫咪视频流口水。

sentences.en: So the takeaway that we'll touch on later and throughout this video is this does what you consume or create lead to a beneficial behavior change in yourself and others, or are you unconsciously soaking in information that silently makes your life worse and poisons the information environment by what you contribute to it?
sentences.zh: 所以我们稍后会在视频中深入探讨的要点是：你消费或创造的东西，是否导致了自己和他人有益的行为改变？还是你在无意识地吸收那些悄悄让你生活变糟的信息，并通过你的贡献毒害信息环境？

sentences.en: So that's just layer one.
sentences.zh: 这只是第一层。

sentences.en: Now, as a very quick reminder, the build a two hour content system in 14 days.
sentences.zh: 快速提醒一下，14 天内构建一个两小时内容系统。

sentences.en: I know that's a heck of a name for a cohort slash challenge that starts very soon.
sentences.zh: 我知道这个名字对于一个即将开始的训练营/挑战来说有点夸张。

sentences.en: I put out this video a bit too late, so you're on the timer link in the description if you want to join that.
sentences.zh: 我这个视频发得有点晚了，所以如果你想加入，倒计时已经开始，链接在简介里。

sentences.en: So if you are interested in turning intentional, thoughtful writing into some form of a career or side income, or simply realize that you do have ideas worth putting out into the public, consider joining before the start date.
sentences.zh: 如果你有兴趣把有意识、有深度的写作变成某种职业或副业收入，或者只是意识到自己确实有值得公开分享的想法，考虑在开始日期前加入。

sentences.en: Now that leads to point number two, which are the three forces breaking civilization's ability to think?
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第二点，也就是破坏文明思考能力的三种力量。

sentences.en: Another quote from Daniel Berger as technology is empowering our choices and we are getting something like the power of gods.
sentences.zh: 引用 Daniel Berger 的另一句话：技术正在赋能我们的选择，我们正在获得类似神的力量。

sentences.en: You have to have something like the love and the wisdom of gods to wield that, or you self-destruct.
sentences.zh: 你必须拥有类似神的爱与智慧才能驾驭它，否则你就会自我毁灭。

sentences.en: So with that quote, I want to finally introduce you to who I think is one of the greatest thinkers of our time, Daniel Berger.
sentences.zh: 借由这句话，我想终于向你介绍一位我认为是我们这个时代最伟大的思想家之一，Daniel Berger。

sentences.en: He doesn't post much on social media.
sentences.zh: 他在社交媒体上不怎么发东西。

sentences.en: I think he hasn't posted in years, actually, but he does make the occasional appearance on a podcast.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我觉得他已经好几年没发过东西了，但他偶尔会在播客上露面。

sentences.en: If you just search for him on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 你只要在 YouTube 上搜他就行。

sentences.en: But when you listen to them, you can instantly tell that he has a very deep and profound thinker that is calm, nuanced and non polarizing.
sentences.zh: 但当你听他们对话时，你能立刻感觉到他是一个非常深邃、深刻的思想者，冷静、细腻，而且不制造对立。

sentences.en: And he has dedicated his life to what he calls the meta crisis.
sentences.zh: 他把自己的一生献给了他所说的"元危机"。

sentences.en: And while it's much deeper than what we're talking about in this video of just posting content on social media or writing essays, that's what we're personally focused on here, because that's what I want to talk about today.
sentences.zh: 虽然这比我们在这个视频里讲的——只是在社交媒体上发内容或写文章——要深刻得多，但那是我们在这里个人关注的重点，因为这就是我今天想聊的。

sentences.en: So in a nutshell, Daniel Neuberger believes that there are three converging forces that can result in three different outcomes, two of those outcomes being catastrophic in the three forces that are converging or threats to civilization in society.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，Daniel Neuberger 认为有三种汇聚的力量，可能导致三种不同的结果，其中两种是灾难性的，而这三种汇聚的力量是对文明和社会的威胁。

sentences.en: So the three threats or what he calls generator functions, or first rivalrous dynamics, which are win lose games where one party's gain requires another's loss.
sentences.zh: 这三种威胁，或者他所说的"生成函数"，首先是竞争性动态，也就是零和博弈，一方的获益需要另一方的损失。

sentences.en: So think arms races or corporate competition, or social media content and academic publishing like hoarding data to publish first.
sentences.zh: 想想军备竞赛、企业竞争，或者社交媒体内容和学术发表，比如为了抢先发表而囤积数据。

sentences.en: The second is substrate consumption.
sentences.zh: 第二个是基质消耗。

sentences.en: Substrate is what something needs to exist, like soil for plants, attention for media, or trust for markets.
sentences.zh: 基质是某物存在所需的东西，比如植物需要土壤，媒体需要注意力，市场需要信任。

sentences.en: When systems consume their foundation faster than they can regenerate, that's bad.
sentences.zh: 当系统消耗其基础的速度快于其再生速度时，那就糟了。

sentences.en: So you can think depleting topsoil that took millennia to form and the attention economy consuming human cognitive capacity faster than it recovers.
sentences.zh: 你可以想想耗尽需要数千年才能形成的表层土壤，以及注意力经济消耗人类认知能力的速度快于其恢复速度。

sentences.en: And the third threat is exponential technology.
sentences.zh: 第三个威胁是指数级技术。

sentences.en: So tools and systems that improve themselves at accelerating rates, outpacing human wisdom.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些以加速度自我改进、超越人类智慧的工具和系统。

sentences.en: You can think AI doubling in capacity, automated weapons and social media algorithms evolving faster than we can study their psychological impacts.
sentences.zh: 你可以想想能力翻倍的 AI、自动化武器，以及进化速度超过我们研究其心理影响速度的社交媒体算法。

sentences.en: So when those three things converge, they can result in civilizational collapse.
sentences.zh: 当这三者汇聚时，它们可能导致文明崩溃。

sentences.en: So nuclear war, unaligned AI, ecological destruction or engineered pandemics, or outside of civilizational collapse, they can result in dystopian control.
sentences.zh: 比如核战争、失控的 AI、生态破坏或人造流行病；或者在文明崩溃之外，它们可能导致反乌托邦式的控制。

sentences.en: So think total surveillance just being surveilled all the time or digital authoritarianism, or just the elimination of agency in the ability to make your own choices.
sentences.zh: 想想全面监控，无时无刻不被监视，或者数字威权主义，或者仅仅是自主选择能力的丧失。

sentences.en: So he calls these two outcomes attractors.
sentences.zh: 他把这两种结果称为"吸引子"。

sentences.en: Those are the two attractors that we're trying to avoid heading towards.
sentences.zh: 那是我们试图避免滑向的两个吸引子。

sentences.en: And they are kind of like the basins that a lot of complex societies already fall into.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像很多复杂社会已经陷入的盆地。

sentences.en: If you look around the world now, the third attractor or the good outcome, here is a world where sense making, shared understanding and aligned incentives exist.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在环顾世界，第三个吸引子，也就是好的结果，是一个意义建构、共同理解和激励对齐都存在的世界。

sentences.en: Now, when we look at the internet, AI and social media, it's pretty easy to see this playing out.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们审视互联网、AI 和社交媒体时，很容易看到这一切正在上演。

sentences.en: As an example, content creators compete for attention so they optimize for engagement rather than transformation, which is the rivalrous dynamics part.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，内容创作者争夺注意力，所以他们优化的是互动而非转变，这就是竞争性动态的部分。

sentences.en: Because the algorithm doesn't measure transformation, it measures how much someone viewed the thing or liked the thing or shared the thing.
sentences.zh: 因为算法不衡量转变，它衡量的是有多少人观看了这个东西、点赞了或分享了。

sentences.en: So creators are much more likely to abandon truth or transformation for whatever will make people react.
sentences.zh: 所以创作者更可能为了任何能让人做出反应的东西而放弃真相或转变。

sentences.en: That's an obvious problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个显而易见的问题。

sentences.en: So when engagement is optimized in someone consumes that information.
sentences.zh: 所以当互动被优化，而某人消费了那些信息——

sentences.en: Like you watching this video, it does not require thinking or understanding.
sentences.zh: 就像你正在看这个视频——它不需要思考或理解。

sentences.en: So the viewer's mental muscle thinking muscle atrophies.
sentences.zh: 于是观看者的心智肌肉、思考肌肉就萎缩了。

sentences.en: AI accelerates content production, yes, but it also accelerates imitation.
sentences.zh: AI 加速了内容生产，是的，但它也加速了模仿。

sentences.en: And when there is only destructive content to imitate, you can see where that goes.
sentences.zh: 而当只有破坏性的内容可供模仿时，你能看到那会走向何方。

sentences.en: So AI itself isn't the issue.
sentences.zh: 所以 AI 本身不是问题。

sentences.en: The issue is that it can mimic what looks like real thinking without requiring any cognitive effort from either the creator or the consumer.
sentences.zh: 问题是它能在创作者和消费者都不需要任何认知努力的情况下，模仿出看起来像真正思考的东西。

sentences.en: So the default outcome here is that the epistemic commons, or mental water supply becomes poisoned incredibly fast, because it's optimized for content that looks like it should shift your thinking, but structurally it cannot.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的默认结果是，认知公地，或者说精神水源，会以极快的速度被污染，因为它被优化来产出那些看起来应该能转变你思维的内容，但在结构上它做不到。

sentences.en: So that's layer two, which leads to layer three, which is what you can actually do about it and how you can profit from it in a meaningful way.
sentences.zh: 这是第二层，它引出了第三层，也就是你实际上能对此做些什么，以及你如何以一种有意义的方式从中获利。

sentences.en: So point number three is why essays may be the last bastion of real thinking.
sentences.zh: 第三点是，为什么随笔可能是真正思考的最后堡垒。

sentences.en: In another quote, wisdom is not algorithmic and cannot be made algorithmic.
sentences.zh: 引用另一句话，智慧不是算法的，也无法被算法化。

sentences.en: Now for the past few decades, a certain type of content has dominated the internet, specifically content that delivers conclusions without requiring thought.
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里，某一类内容主导了互联网，具体来说，就是那种只传递结论、不需要你思考的内容。

sentences.en: In other words, it's fast food for the mind.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是精神快餐。

sentences.en: So we're going to call this category of media or information fast content, because social media companies use the same psychological triggers to get you addicted as fast food companies who realized fat, sugar and salt were a scarce good, that our brains aren't wired to have an abundance, finding those resources spike dopamine because they eat it in survival.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将把这类媒体或信息称为"快内容"，因为社交媒体公司用来让你上瘾的心理触发机制，和快餐公司如出一辙——快餐公司发现脂肪、糖和盐是稀缺品，我们的大脑并不适应丰裕状态，找到这些资源会刺激多巴胺分泌，因为在生存环境中它们至关重要。

sentences.en: So, on the fast content end of the spectrum, you have BuzzFeed listicles, rage tweets, AI generated summaries, hot takes, engagement optimized threads, and TikTok explainers.
sentences.zh: 在快内容这一端，你有 BuzzFeed 的清单体、愤怒推文、AI 生成的摘要、热辣点评、为互动量优化的推文串，以及 TikTok 上的科普解说。

sentences.en: They give you the feeling of understanding in 30s. It makes sense why everyone thinks they're an expert these days.
sentences.zh: 它们在 30 秒内给你一种"我懂了"的感觉。难怪现在每个人都觉得自己是专家。

sentences.en: Now, on the slow content end of the spectrum, or content that requires you to think and potentially change your behavior, you have essays, long form non optimized conversations, certain books, certain lectures, and even tweets crafted in a way that make you think to receive the insight.
sentences.zh: 而在慢内容这一端，也就是那些要求你思考并可能改变你行为的内容，你有随笔、未经优化的长对话、某些书、某些讲座，甚至是以一种让你必须思考才能获得洞见的方式精心写就的推文。

sentences.en: Now, I personally want to focus on essays, but all of this type of content is good and that's actually what we go over in the challenge that I mentioned link in the description.
sentences.zh: 我个人想聚焦在随笔上，但所有这些类型的内容都是好的，这实际上也是我在简介里提到的那个挑战中会详细讲的内容。

sentences.en: So why essays?
sentences.zh: 那为什么是随笔？

sentences.en: Because they are something that you can produce alone and leverage to take advantage of the meaning economy we're heading into.
sentences.zh: 因为它是你可以独自产出，并利用它来抓住我们正在进入的意义经济的东西。

sentences.en: And essays are the most scalable and durable form.
sentences.zh: 而且随笔是最具可扩展性和持久性的形式。

sentences.en: A meaningful conversation can shift one person, but it lives and dies in the memory of the participants.
sentences.zh: 一场有意义的对话可以转变一个人，但它的生命始于也终于参与者的记忆。

sentences.en: An essay develops the readers and writers thinking capacity, and it can do that for thousands of people across thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 一篇随笔能发展读者和写作者的思考能力，而且它可以跨越数千年，对成千上万的人做到这一点。

sentences.en: More on that in a bit.
sentences.zh: 这个稍后再说。

sentences.en: And on top of that, most people, including me, including you, walk around with opinions that they've never thought through.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，大多数人，包括我，包括你，都带着一些自己从未深思过的观点走来走去。

sentences.en: They feel like they believe something, but they've never sat down and tried to write out exactly what they believe in.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉自己相信某件事，但从未坐下来，试着把自己到底相信什么写清楚。

sentences.en: The especially haven't tried to write it down in a way that would survive a smart person's criticism.
sentences.zh: 他们尤其没有试着用一种能经得起聪明人批评的方式把它写下来。

sentences.en: And it also doesn't hurt that some of the world's most respected minds were forged through the act of writing essays.
sentences.zh: 而且，世界上一些最受尊敬的头脑正是通过写随笔这个行为锻造出来的，这也没什么坏处。

sentences.en: So Paul Graham for the tech pros, or Isaac Newton for the science prose, or Jordan Peterson in his prime, or Nietzsche or Emerson, or a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 比如科技界的 Paul Graham，科学界的 Isaac Newton，巅峰时期的 Jordan Peterson，或者 Nietzsche，或者 Emerson，很多人。

sentences.en: The defining factor of an essay is that I cannot write one now for understanding what an essay actually is.
sentences.zh: 一篇随笔的决定性因素是，我现在没法为了理解随笔到底是什么而去写一篇。

sentences.en: It helps to distinguish an essay from an article, articles or answers, while essays or arguments articles package existing knowledge, while essays change the author's beliefs, articles start with the conclusion, while essays figure it out.
sentences.zh: 区分随笔和文章会很有帮助，文章是答案，而随笔是论证；文章打包已有知识，而随笔改变作者的信念；文章从结论开始，而随笔在写作中理清结论。

sentences.en: Articles inform or educate.
sentences.zh: 文章提供信息或教育。

sentences.en: While essays are an act of thinking, articles communicate what's already there, while essays discover what isn't. Now, this video isn't to say that you should never write an article, and it's also not to say that essays and articles don't overlap in some way.
sentences.zh: 而随笔是一种思考行为，文章传达已经存在的东西，而随笔发现还不存在的东西。这个视频并不是说你永远不该写文章，也不是说随笔和文章没有任何重叠。

sentences.en: What I'm trying to say is that you should write with the intention of refining what you believe in, actually impacting the other person on the other side.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你应该带着精炼你所相信的东西、真正影响屏幕另一边那个人的意图去写。

sentences.en: Now, if you think about it, only a human can write an essay because a robot doesn't have a situated point of view, it does not have direct experience.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，只有人类能写随笔，因为机器人没有一个具身化的视角，它没有直接经验。

sentences.en: It can simulate the perspective you tell it to adopt, but it lacks the beliefs, biases, and emotions that lead you to think and question in a particular direction.
sentences.zh: 它可以模拟你让它采用的视角，但它缺乏那些引导你朝特定方向思考和质疑的信念、偏见和情感。

sentences.en: And honestly, I use AI a lot.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我用 AI 很多。

sentences.en: It would be nearly impossible to pass off all of that context.
sentences.zh: 要把所有这些上下文都传递给它几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: It would need to be hooked into your brain like Neuralink at all times, in order to understand every passing moment, every experience.
sentences.zh: 它需要像 Neuralink 那样一直连接着你的大脑，才能理解每一个流逝的瞬间、每一次经历。

sentences.en: How you get information.
sentences.zh: 你怎么获取信息。

sentences.en: It would have to understand all of your memories, all of your unconscious, everything that leads to you being who you are today.
sentences.zh: 它得理解你所有的记忆，你所有的潜意识，所有让你成为今天这个人的一切。

sentences.en: That's why I've been saying for the longest time that you are the niche.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我一直说，你自己就是那个细分领域。

sentences.en: You are the most valuable resource, your point of view.
sentences.zh: 你是最有价值的资源，你的视角。

sentences.en: I've talked about that in multiple videos, so I doesn't have access to that, because every passing moment influences your point of view.
sentences.zh: 我在好几个视频里都讲过这个，所以它做不到，因为每一个流逝的瞬间都在影响你的视角。

sentences.en: And in order to have a meaningful point of view worth writing about or we're talking about, you can't be sitting at your desk all day on Claud 24 over seven.
sentences.zh: 而要拥有一个值得写、值得讨论的有意义的视角，你不能一天到晚坐在桌前，24小时泡在Claude里。

sentences.en: You have to engage in novel experiences. You have to live life.
sentences.zh: 你必须去经历新鲜的事。你必须去生活。

sentences.en: You can't live.
sentences.zh: 你不能过那种

sentences.en: The optimized, efficient productivity life of just staring at your laptop all day.
sentences.zh: 优化过的、高效的、生产力至上的生活，整天只盯着笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: So while everyone is just locked in to the agents, the new agents, the open floor, getting them to just build a bunch of nonsense that is going to get them nowhere, you have to actually reject that.
sentences.zh: 所以当所有人都沉迷于那些智能体、新出的智能体、开放平台，让它们去建一堆毫无意义的垃圾、根本带他们去不了任何地方的时候，你必须拒绝这些。

sentences.en: Go out, experience life, build a good life, and then bring that online because nobody else is doing that.
sentences.zh: 走出去，体验生活，构建一个好的人生，然后把它带到线上，因为没有别人在做这件事。

sentences.en: That's how you become unique.
sentences.zh: 这才是你变得独一无二的方式。

sentences.en: And now I think the more important point here is that I've recently realized that I destroys the magic of surprise and discovery.
sentences.zh: 而我现在觉得更重要的一点是，我最近意识到，AI摧毁了惊喜和发现的魔力。

sentences.en: In other words, it destroys creativity.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它摧毁了创造力。

sentences.en: Sure, I can be creative in some ways, but this is a crucial point.
sentences.zh: 当然，AI在某些方面可以很有创造力，但这是一个关键点。

sentences.en: You can tell AI to share something novel, but then you are anticipating it.
sentences.zh: 你可以让AI分享一些新颖的东西，但这时候你已经在期待它了。

sentences.en: It is no longer novel.
sentences.zh: 它就不再新颖了。

sentences.en: It's no longer surprise you destroyed any chance of stumbling upon a discovery.
sentences.zh: 它不再让你惊喜，你摧毁了任何偶然发现的机会。

sentences.en: In other words, you destroyed any chance of actually discovering it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你摧毁了真正发现它的任何可能。

sentences.en: It may give you good material to write about, but it was not from your own creative ability and thinking.
sentences.zh: 它可能会给你很好的写作素材，但那不是来自你自己的创造能力和思考。

sentences.en: So the more I use AI, the more useful I find it, because it's incredibly useful.
sentences.zh: 所以我越用AI，越觉得它有用，因为它确实极其有用。

sentences.en: But on the other edge of the sword, I find that it exhausts creativity extremely fast because creativity is kind of sparse.
sentences.zh: 但在剑的另一刃上，我发现它极快地耗尽创造力，因为创造力本来就是稀缺的。

sentences.en: Again, it requires you to go out, do things, experience something novel, and then you have a little bit to write about.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，它需要你走出去，做事情，经历一些新颖的东西，然后你才有一点东西可写。

sentences.en: But with AI you can just give it to the AI and then it does everything for you.
sentences.zh: 但有了AI，你可以直接丢给AI，然后它帮你做完一切。

sentences.en: And now, like you are empty creatively, you didn't take the time to actually sit with it, understand it, think through it.
sentences.zh: 这时候，你在创造力上是空的，你没有花时间去真正坐下来消化它、理解它、想透它。

sentences.en: So as someone who is still very pro AI, I can't help but believe that the most relevant content on the internet going forward will be in essay form, solo content.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个仍然非常支持AI的人，我不得不相信，未来互联网上最相关的内容，会是文章形式、单人创作的内容。

sentences.en: And I don't only mean long form, I mean anything that is the opposite of what an article is like.
sentences.zh: 我不只是指长内容，我指的是任何和AI生成的文章相反的东西。

sentences.en: We went over.
sentences.zh: 我们之前讲过。

sentences.en: So that leads to point number four, which is about the meaning economy and how to thrive in it.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第四点，关于意义经济以及如何在其中蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: So we talked about this in a future video that was called The Future of Work and the New high income skill stack, and it got a decent amount of views, but I still think it's vastly underrated and more people should go watch it.
sentences.zh: 我们在一个叫《工作的未来和新高收入技能栈》的视频里聊过这个，那个视频播放量还不错，但我仍然觉得它被严重低估了，更多人应该去看。

sentences.en: It's like five videos ago that I posted, but in that video I talk about the meaning economy.
sentences.zh: 大概是我发的五个视频之前，但在那个视频里我谈到了意义经济。

sentences.en: And this meaning economy, so to say, has been emerging for a few years now, and AI has only accelerated this and made this more of a thing.
sentences.zh: 而这个所谓的意义经济，已经出现了好几年，AI只是加速了这个过程，让它变得更显著。

sentences.en: I would argue that I'm a part of the meaning economy and many value creators, which we'll touch on in a bit, form this meaning economy, or at least the starts of it.
sentences.zh: 我会说我是意义经济的一部分，很多价值创造者——我们待会儿会讲到——构成了这个意义经济，或者至少是它的开端。

sentences.en: So why is this important?
sentences.zh: 那么这为什么重要？

sentences.en: Because meaning is the scarcest commodity in civilization right now.
sentences.zh: 因为意义是当今文明中最稀缺的商品。

sentences.en: Before industrialization, we praised gods in the sky.
sentences.zh: 工业化之前，我们赞美天上的神。

sentences.en: During industrialization, we made productivity. Are God.
sentences.zh: 工业化时代，我们把生产力当成了神。

sentences.en: Today more is our God.
sentences.zh: 今天，“更多”是我们的神。

sentences.en: More money, more information, more content.
sentences.zh: 更多钱、更多信息、更多内容。

sentences.en: We have more stuff and less purpose than ever.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的东西比以往任何时候都多，但目标感却比以往任何时候都少。

sentences.en: So in my eyes, meaning will be sold at a premium.
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，意义会以极高的溢价出售。

sentences.en: People will crave it more than they already do because most people in today's world feel lonely, feel empty, feel like they don't have any purpose, feel like they're not working towards anything greater than themselves.
sentences.zh: 人们会比现在更渴望它，因为当今世界的大多数人感到孤独、感到空虚、感觉自己没有任何目标、感觉自己没有在为任何超越自我的事情努力。

sentences.en: They're just stuck on their computer all day, hoping that pulling the eye slot machine or doing the repetitive tasks that they were assigned leads to something good.
sentences.zh: 他们只是整天困在电脑前，希望拉动眼球老虎机，或者完成分配给他们的重复性任务，能带来什么好结果。

sentences.en: And so who better to provide that meaning than those who shape the epistemic commons or the mental water supply, or the information environment?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁能比那些塑造认知公共空间、或者塑造精神水源、或者塑造信息环境的人，更适合提供这种意义呢？

sentences.en: It's the value creators who fight against the poisoning of the water supply.
sentences.zh: 是那些价值创造者在对抗水源的毒化。

sentences.en: Now the question is how is meaning created or experienced?
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，意义是如何被创造或体验的？

sentences.en: Because we need to understand that before we can actually replicate it.
sentences.zh: 因为我们需要先理解这一点，才能真正复制它。

sentences.en: I guess when attention is fragmented, scattered, and pulled in competing directions, that's psychic entropy.
sentences.zh: 我想，当注意力被碎片化、被分散、被拉向相互竞争的方向时，那就是精神熵。

sentences.en: It feels like anxiety, boredom, and restlessness.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像焦虑、无聊和躁动不安。

sentences.en: It's chaos when attention is invested in a complex, challenging activity with clear feedback that psychic neg entropy.
sentences.zh: 那是混乱。当注意力被投入到一项复杂、有挑战性、且反馈清晰的活动时，那就是精神负熵。

sentences.en: It feels like flow, purpose and meaning.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像心流、目标感和意义。

sentences.en: It's order.
sentences.zh: 那是秩序。

sentences.en: So meaning isn't something you find out there in the world.
sentences.zh: 所以意义不是你在外部世界找到的东西。

sentences.en: It's a state of consciousness that emerges when your attention is ordered towards something complex enough to fully engage you.
sentences.zh: 它是一种意识状态，当你的注意力被有序地导向某个足够复杂、足以完全吸引你的事物时，它就会涌现。

sentences.en: If you are level ten, a level one challenge is boring, and a level 20 challenge is daunting.
sentences.zh: 如果你是十级，一级的挑战很无聊，二十级的挑战令人畏惧。

sentences.en: But a level 11 challenge is just enough to lock you in.
sentences.zh: 但十一级的挑战刚好能把你锁定。

sentences.en: So in other words, meaning is the experience of ordered consciousness.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，意义就是有序意识的体验。

sentences.en: Now, along the same vein, meaning is created through the process of ordering consciousness, the act of ordering consciousness or taking chaos and creating structure or wrestling with complexity until it coheres results in meaning.
sentences.zh: 同样地，意义是通过整理意识的过程创造出来的，整理意识的行为，或者说把混乱变成结构，或者与复杂性搏斗直到它凝聚成形，这个过程会产生意义。

sentences.en: Obviously, if the experience of ordered consciousness is meaningful.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果有序意识的体验是有意义的。

sentences.en: So if you've ever been stuck in a rut or wrestled with where your life should go and eventually receive this like burst of clarity that launches you into this intense season of life, you've directly experience this.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经陷入低谷，或者苦苦思索自己的人生该往哪里走，最终获得一种突然的清晰感，把你推入一段高强度的人生阶段，你就直接体验过这一点。

sentences.en: So what does this have to do with content, essays, writing, etc.?
sentences.zh: 那么，这和内容、文章、写作等等有什么关系？

sentences.en: One is that fast content or entropic pre digested algorithmic AI generated content skips the ordering process and delivers prepackaged conclusions.
sentences.zh: 第一，快内容，或者说高熵的、预消化的、算法生成的、AI 生成的内容，跳过了整理过程，直接交付打包好的结论。

sentences.en: The reader's consciousness stays and becomes more disordered.
sentences.zh: 读者的意识保持混乱，并且变得更加混乱。

sentences.en: They received information but didn't generate meaning.
sentences.zh: 他们接收了信息，但没有生成意义。

sentences.en: That's why they feel informed.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们感觉自己见多识广。

sentences.en: But empty too.
sentences.zh: 但同时也感到空虚。

sentences.en: Is that slow content.
sentences.zh: 第二，慢内容。

sentences.en: So essays genuine thinking in public or insight that requires effort requires both the writer and the reader to engage in the ordering process.
sentences.zh: 所以文章、公开的真诚思考、或者需要付出努力的洞见，要求作者和读者都参与到整理过程中。

sentences.en: The writer orders their own consciousness through the act of writing.
sentences.zh: 写作者通过写作这个过程，整理自己的意识。

sentences.en: The reader reorders their thoughts by properly digesting the thinking.
sentences.zh: 读者通过认真消化这些思考，重新整理自己的思绪。

sentences.en: So what's the opportunity here?
sentences.zh: 所以，机会在哪里？

sentences.en: The main thing is that the world doesn't need more rage bait posters and mainstream news channels.
sentences.zh: 重点是，这个世界不需要更多引战帖和主流新闻频道。

sentences.en: It also doesn't need more people competing to become the most productive person in the world, and trying to build the next billion dollar AI company.
sentences.zh: 也不需要更多人挤破头去争当世界上最高效的人，或者试图打造下一个十亿美元的 AI 公司。

sentences.en: Instead, it needs ordinary people who make sense of their own minds and document them in public.
sentences.zh: 相反，它需要的是普通人——能理清自己的头脑，并公开记录这个过程。

sentences.en: Now, previously, I've called these types of people value creators.
sentences.zh: 之前，我把这类人称为价值创造者。

sentences.en: I quite literally have a video called The Value Creator or The rise of the Value Creator, and now I call them value creators because they're very distinct from your typical influencer or personal brand.
sentences.zh: 我确实做过一期视频，就叫《价值创造者》，或者说《价值创造者的崛起》。我这么叫他们，是因为他们和你通常看到的网红或个人品牌截然不同。

sentences.en: It's a person who chooses a positive trajectory for their life, cares deeply about the interests and skills that help move the needle toward that, and passes their journey down from their point of view to others who can relate and benefit from it.
sentences.zh: 这种人会为自己的人生选择一条积极的轨道，深切关注那些能推动自己向前的兴趣和技能，并把自己的旅程，从自己的视角传递出去，让那些能产生共鸣、能从中受益的人看到。

sentences.en: By all measures, I believe this is a futureproof and deeply meaningful way to live.
sentences.zh: 无论从哪个角度看，我都相信这是一种面向未来的、极其有意义的生活方式。

sentences.en: Sure, you weren't creating a tangible physical product to show that you've actually done something, or that you have a real job, but you are causing a greater cascade.
sentences.zh: 没错，你没有创造出一个看得见摸得着的实体产品，来证明你真的做了什么，或者你有一份"正经工作"，但你在引发一场更大的连锁反应。

sentences.en: That is, you are providing the route.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你在提供路线。

sentences.en: You're providing the information that influences identity, that influences behavior, that influences the flourishing or destruction of civilization.
sentences.zh: 你在提供信息，这些信息影响身份认同，影响行为，进而影响文明的繁荣或毁灭。

sentences.en: And in my eyes, even building rockets isn't that impactful.
sentences.zh: 在我眼里，连造火箭都没这么大的影响力。

sentences.en: That's honestly why I do what I do.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这就是我做这件事的原因。

sentences.en: Or maybe not why I chose to do this.
sentences.zh: 或者说，也许不是我选择做这件事的原因。

sentences.en: I kind of stumbled upon it, but I found that this was just a deeply meaningful way to live.
sentences.zh: 我算是误打误撞进来的，但我发现这真的是一种极其有意义的生活方式。

sentences.en: It's very purposeful. It feels good.
sentences.zh: 非常有目标感。感觉很好。

sentences.en: So that leads to point number five, which is how to think in public and why it's the most valuable skill you can develop.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第五点：如何公开思考，以及为什么它是你能培养的最有价值的技能。

sentences.en: Now, it's kind of funny here because with this video it's just a polished package, right.
sentences.zh: 说起来有点好笑，因为这期视频只是一个精心包装后的成品，对吧。

sentences.en: There's cuts that cut out everything but the outline of this video or the newsletter.
sentences.zh: 视频里剪掉了一切，只留下了这期视频或者说那期 newsletter 的大纲。

sentences.en: Subscribe to my Substack if you want these before they go out on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在 YouTube 发布之前看到这些内容，可以订阅我的 Substack。

sentences.en: This was incredibly difficult to write and just think through.
sentences.zh: 写这篇稿子、把它想清楚，真的极其困难。

sentences.en: I actually had three other drafts of Why You Should Write Essays that I scrapped entirely, because they just didn't feel right.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我之前写过三版完全不同的《为什么你应该写文章》，但全被我扔掉了，因为感觉就是不对。

sentences.en: But by sticking with the challenge and really trying to synthesize a point of view that I actually aligned with and that I felt was true and impactful has changed my mind.
sentences.zh: 但通过坚持这个挑战，真正尝试去合成一个我自己认同、觉得真实且有影响力的观点，这件事改变了我。

sentences.en: It's helped me articulate and cohere or make something coherent in my mind.
sentences.zh: 它帮我清晰地表达出来，让一些东西在我脑子里变得连贯、自洽。

sentences.en: And if this video changes your mind or your behavior in some way, that brings even more meaning into my life and yours.
sentences.zh: 如果这期视频在某种程度上改变了你的想法或行为，那就会给我和你的人生带来更多意义。

sentences.en: And now I hope you can experience that same feeling.
sentences.zh: 现在，我希望你也能体验到那种感觉。

sentences.en: So we need to get a bit practical here.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们得聊点实操了。

sentences.en: I want you to try writing your first essay of some form, even if it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 我希望你试着写你的第一篇文章，不管什么形式，哪怕很难。

sentences.en: It's supposed to be difficult, especially if you're not a writer.
sentences.zh: 它本来就该很难，尤其是如果你不是写作者的话。

sentences.en: So I put a few points together.
sentences.zh: 所以我整理了几点。

sentences.en: These are going to be rapid fire, so it's not too long.
sentences.zh: 我会讲得很快，不会太长。

sentences.en: But this should get you started, right?
sentences.zh: 但这些应该能帮你起步，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't need that much to just start with.
sentences.zh: 你其实不需要太多东西就能开始。

sentences.en: Take out a piece of paper and start writing, or to open up an app and start writing.
sentences.zh: 拿出一张纸开始写，或者打开一个 App 开始写。

sentences.en: So here's how you write an essay.
sentences.zh: 下面来说怎么写一篇 essay。

sentences.en: First is write to discover, not to perform.
sentences.zh: 第一，为发现而写，不要为表演而写。

sentences.en: Because most social media engagement comes from packaging anyway, and you can learn about that later.
sentences.zh: 因为社交媒体上大部分互动靠的本来就是包装，这个你以后可以再学。

sentences.en: So start with a concept, viewpoint, question, experience, thought, or something that bothers you or just a topic.
sentences.zh: 所以，从一个概念、一个观点、一个问题、一段经历、一个想法，或者某个让你不爽的事情，甚至只是一个话题开始。

sentences.en: An essay begins with uncertainty and an open mind.
sentences.zh: 一篇 essay 始于不确定和开放的心态。

sentences.en: Two is right about what genuinely interests you.
sentences.zh: 第二，写你真正感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: Focus on a single main idea.
sentences.zh: 聚焦在一个核心想法上。

sentences.en: Use this as a time to research and learn.
sentences.zh: 把这段时间当作研究和学习的机会。

sentences.en: Go down rabbit holes. Challenge everyone's point of view.
sentences.zh: 去钻兔子洞，去挑战所有人的观点。

sentences.en: Do not accept one source as law three.
sentences.zh: 不要把任何一个来源当成铁律。

sentences.en: Resist the template.
sentences.zh: 第三，抵抗模板。

sentences.en: You'll find how you like to structure your writing as you get better at it.
sentences.zh: 随着你越写越好，你会找到自己喜欢的结构方式。

sentences.en: It's a skill.
sentences.zh: 这是一项技能。

sentences.en: Remember that. But for now, just write.
sentences.zh: 记住这一点。但现在，只管写。

sentences.en: Have a debate with yourself.
sentences.zh: 和自己辩论。

sentences.en: Ask questions to keep the writing going.
sentences.zh: 用提问来让写作持续下去。

sentences.en: Then worry about the structure and ask for help if you want.
sentences.zh: 之后再操心结构，需要的话可以找人帮忙。

sentences.en: Do the thinking first for ask.
sentences.zh: 第四，先做思考。

sentences.en: Do I actually believe this?
sentences.zh: 我真的相信这个吗？

sentences.en: It's easy to write what you already believe, but the point of this is to change what you believe.
sentences.zh: 写你已经相信的东西很容易，但这件事的意义在于改变你所相信的。

sentences.en: This is the most difficult part.
sentences.zh: 这是最难的部分。

sentences.en: Resist the urge to act like you are absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 克制那种表现得自己绝对正确的冲动。

sentences.en: Five read essays and consume central content.
sentences.zh: 第五，读 essay，消费核心内容。

sentences.en: Your sense making capacity is shaped by your inputs.
sentences.zh: 你的意义构建能力由你的输入塑造。

sentences.en: You can't expect the for you page to feed you this content.
sentences.zh: 你不能指望推荐页给你推送这些内容。

sentences.en: You must actively search, curate and nurture your digital feed.
sentences.zh: 你必须主动搜索、筛选和培育你的信息流。

sentences.en: Six build a body of work, not a content calendar.
sentences.zh: 第六，构建一个作品体系，而不是一个内容日历。

sentences.en: People don't follow creators for one piece of content they follow for their body of coherent work.
sentences.zh: 人们关注一个创作者不是因为某一篇内容，而是因为他们那一整套连贯的作品。

sentences.en: Each essay compounds on the last.
sentences.zh: 每一篇 essay 都在上一篇的基础上叠加。

sentences.en: I can't replicate a coherent philosophy built through years of genuine thinking, so that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我无法复制一个通过多年真诚思考构建出来的连贯哲学，这很好理解。

sentences.en: But where do you start?
sentences.zh: 但你要从哪里开始？

sentences.en: If you actually want to do this online, I would recommend ECS or Substack because that's where you're really seeing the revival of long form content.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想在线上做这件事，我会推荐 ECS 或 Substack，因为那里你才能真正看到长内容正在复兴。

sentences.en: I mean, I was runner up in the $1 million challenge of the articles when they brought articles back in mind, went insanely viral.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当 Medium 重新推出文章功能时，我在百万美元挑战赛中拿了亚军，那篇文章疯传得离谱。

sentences.en: Substack, I think, is the most slept on social media right now because one, you own your audience, people who follow or subscribe to you, you have a list of them too.
sentences.zh: Substack 我觉得是现在最被低估的社交媒体，因为第一，你拥有自己的受众，关注或订阅你的人，你也有一份他们的名单。

sentences.en: It's email first, and if you understand anything about newsletters or email marketing, you understand how powerful that is.
sentences.zh: 它是邮件优先的，如果你对 newsletter 或邮件营销有任何了解，你就知道这有多强大。

sentences.en: And three, they have a notes feed of people who actually appreciate deep and genuine thinking.
sentences.zh: 第三，它有一个笔记信息流，里面的人是真的欣赏深度和真诚思考的。

sentences.en: So if you need somewhere to write, I just start with Substack or X, depending on which one you vibe with the most.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你需要找个地方写，就从 Substack 或 X 开始吧，看你跟哪个更合拍。

sentences.en: Now, I've written about that in my newsletter, and I've talked about it in multiple videos before, so we're going to leave it at that.
sentences.zh: 这个我在自己的 newsletter 里写过，之前的视频也聊过好几次，所以我们就说到这。

sentences.en: I think that's enough.
sentences.zh: 我觉得够了。

sentences.en: And again, if you want a guided challenge to do this and you want to understand frameworks for writing and how to generate or capture ideas, or how to just figure out what you want to talk about or how to phrase things in an impactful way.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，如果你想要一个有引导的挑战来做这件事，想理解写作的框架、怎么生成或捕捉想法，或者怎么搞清楚你想聊什么、怎么把话说得有冲击力。

sentences.en: Then consider joining the build a two hour content system in 14 days challenge that starts very, very soon because I got this video out late.
sentences.zh: 那可以考虑加入"14 天构建两小时内容系统"挑战，很快就开始了，因为这期视频我发晚了。

sentences.en: Link in the description for that.
sentences.zh: 链接在简介里。

sentences.en: If you don't join that, at least like and subscribe if you like this video and I'll see you in the next one. Bye.
sentences.zh: 如果你不加入，至少点个赞、订阅一下，如果你喜欢这期视频的话，下期见。拜。
